# The Python packages the questionnaire PDF importers need at run time: pypdf and
# the one dependency it pulls below Python 3.11. Installed with --require-hashes
# and --only-binary=:all:, so pip accepts only these exact releases and checks
# every wheel against a hash here before it is unpacked.
#
# Kept apart from the XLSX publishers' packages (runtime-xlsx-requirements.txt)
# because pip verifies a whole requirements file in hash mode: naming one package
# on the command line is refused for having no hash of its own, so a set that
# must be installable on its own needs its own file. pypdf stays the operator's
# to install -- most runs never import a questionnaire -- which is exactly why it
# cannot share a file with openpyxl. Dependabot (the pip ecosystem for /.github,
# weekly, 7-day cooldown) proposes new versions with new hashes.
#
# Install-TPPrerequisites.ps1 reads the version of each package from the file
# that pins it and installs from that same file; the SBOM generator and the docs
# must agree with it (TP.RuntimePins.Tests.ps1 checks).

pypdf==6.20.1 \
    --hash=sha256:aa5a55ddcffdc5e5ab291d5decb23f6383f4e56f8e3263dc39af41fff03885ad \
    --hash=sha256:28f5a9d2fdc2749264612d94e6a58de54c11d730d9f0cabf8ad34117c4942b45
typing_extensions==4.16.0 ; python_version < "3.11" \
    --hash=sha256:481caa481374e813c1b176ada14e97f1f67a4539ce9cfeb3f350d78d6370c2e8 \
    --hash=sha256:dc983d19a509c94dba722ee6abd33940f7c05a89e243c47e907eb4db6f1a43e5
